episodes.172183: A tropical wave moved across the area, increasing convergence at the lower levels. Later in the period, low level moisture was provided by the proximity of a surface trough. Additionally, an upper level low approached from the northeast, providing instability aloft, as high pressure at all level weakened.
episodes.172270: An active monsoon season continued to impact Southern California, with multiple days of thunderstorms reported across the mountains from August 22-26. The main hazards were heavy rain and minor debris flows, as well as gusty winds from thunderstorms.
episodes.172436: Severe weather developed over central into parts of western North Dakota in an environment of enhanced instability and marginal deep layer shear. Many crops were damaged as hail combined with strong wind gusts. The strongest reported wind gust was 76 mph in Mountrail County, while the largest hail was one inch in diameter and occurred with several of the storms in Oliver, McLean, and Mountrail counties. Later in the episode, the focus turned towards flash flooding which occurred in Burleigh County, primarily in and around the city of Bismarck. Vehicles were stranded in flood waters to the south of the North Dakota State Capitol Grounds, and in the 7th Street underpass. Storm sewers were overwhelmed, with manhole covers being pushed off and flood waters escaping.
episodes.172453: A stationary front across Rhode Island and southeast Massachusetts provided the focus for heavy rain and scattered thunderstorms.  Four to six inches of rain fell in the greater Providence area, with a max of 7.44 inches in Rehoboth, MA.
episodes.172454: A stationary front across Rhode Island and southeast Massachusetts provided the focus for heavy rain and scattered thunderstorms.  Four to six inches of rain fell in a portion of southeast Massachusetts, with a max of 7.44 inches in Rehoboth.  An isolated severe thunderstorm occurred in Holyoke in western Massachusetts.
episodes.172455: A stationary front across eastern Connecticut, Rhode Island, and southeast Massachusetts provided the focus for heavy rain and scattered thunderstorms.  One to 2.5 inches of rain fell in northern Connecticut.  A funnel cloud was photographed in eastern Connecticut but no damage was reported at the ground.
episodes.172590: Deep westerly flow prevailed over the region with an upper trough to the north and a ridge axis to the south. The anomalously moist airmass, with PWATs near 2.2 inches, remained over the region. Dense clouds were advected across much of the area Tuesday morning in the westerly flow. Cloudiness limited heating across southeast Georgia whereas northeast Florida experienced breaks in the cloud deck allowing for delayed diurnal destabilization. Storms were diurnally initiated across north central Florida in the afternoon due to less cloud cover over that area. Late start for the sea breezes, with them pushing inland late afternoon into evening.  Weak westerly flow allowed the Atlantic sea breeze to move inland to the St. Johns River basin. Diurnally driven storms in north central Florida lifted north and interacted with the sea breeze boundary in the evening. Slow-moving storms produced heavy rainfall and caused street flooding in Marion, Alachua and Clay counties. These storms produced about 2.5 to 4 inches of rain. A stronger storm in Marion county damaged a metal roof. Another stronger storm produced penny sized hail in Duval. Lightning struck a teenager in Duval causing injuries.
episodes.172822: Showers and thunderstorms developed out ahead of an approaching cold front. Storm coverage and intensity increased as a potent shortwave lifted through the region. Severe storms around the Lehigh Valley formed in the vicinity of a warm front that was bisecting the region.
episodes.173381: An area of low pressure tracked across the region producing scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. One of the storms became severe leading to a downed tree in Saratoga County.
episodes.173415: A cold front that had stalled north of the local area sagged south and became draped across Louisiana and Mississippi. It became the focus for numerous showers and thunderstorms. The combination of daytime heating, a focal point and abundant moisture in place resulted in a couple severe storms over the nearshore coastal waters.
episodes.173432: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front over the area on August 23rd. These thunderstorms were slow moving and produced heavy rainfall over Long Island. The thunderstorms developed in an environment with 1.5 to 1.7 precipitable water and CAPE values of 1500 - 2000 J/kg. The thunderstorms produced locally up to 2 to 3 inches of rain in a 2 hour period.
episodes.173438: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front over the area on August 23rd. These thunderstorms were slow moving and produced heavy rainfall over Connecticut. The thunderstorms developed in an environment with 1.5 to 1.7 inches of precipitable water and CAPE values of 1500 - 2000 J/kg. The thunderstorms produced locally up to 2 to 3 inches of rain in a 2 hour period.
episodes.173443: A front remained nearly stationary over the area. With enough instability, a severe thunderstorm was able to form and produced a waterspout over the waters.
episodes.173444: A front remained nearly stationary over the area. A wave of low pressure developed along the front and dragged a cold front through southeastern CT. Severe thunderstorms developed and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173635: Isolated Severe Thunderstorm moved across northern Red River Valley producing large hail and damaging winds on August 23rd.
episodes.173642: A mid-level high pressure was situated across southern Nevada, with the local area under an northeasterly flow regime. At upper-levels, a disturbance moving northward out northern Baja California resulted in a diffluent flow, favorable for vertical ascent. The moisture and instability parameters were conducive to thunderstorm activity with PWATs 1.5+ inches and MLCAPE values ranging between 1500-2500 J/KG. As it is typical in a northeasterly flow regime, thunderstorms first began to develop along the Mogollon Rim early afternoon and then descended into the lower elevations during the mid to late afternoon hours, affecting the Greater Phoenix area and then tracking southwestward, affecting southwestern Arizona through the early evening hours.
episodes.173686: An elongated upper trough extended through the Borderland.  Deep monsoonal moisture remained in place across the region and when combined with some heavy rain over the previous few days lead to flash flooding in west El Paso.
episodes.173821: Heavy rain upstream in New Mexico caused the Gila River to flood at Duncan, where Highway 70 was closed, and several homes and a couple businesses experienced minor flooding. Downstream at Solomon, the bridge was partially flooded.
episodes.173842: Flash flooding in several national parks and severe hail were observed with scattered thunderstorms.
episodes.173932: A breach in a berm along Rucker Creek near the northeast edge of Elfrida caused flash flooding in part of town on August 23. Additional rainfall in town and upstream of the breach exacerbated the flooding later that day. Heavy rain well upstream traveled downstream through the breach and flooded more of the town on August 24 and 25. Several homes sustained significant flood damage.
episodes.173979: A warm front with moisture laden air moved into the area with dewpoints in the mid 60s to lower 70s. An upper level low slowly moved east through southern New England with a surface low and associated cold front. This supported rounds of convection across the region during the afternoon into the early evening.  A sea breeze front stalled and converged with the warm frontal boundary resulting in a nearly stationary storm with heavy rainfall across southern Maine that produced reports of 4 to 11 inches in York County.  Due to antecedent drought conditions, impacts were limited compared to how much rain fell.
episodes.173999: Deep monsoon moisture and increasing shear produce severe thunderstorms and heavy rain over parts of northern Arizona.
episodes.178461: A low pressure system brought widespread heavy rain to portions of Mississippi with multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms throughout the day on August 23rd.
episodes.178464: A low pressure system spinning over northern Louisiana and southern Arkansas brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms producing widespread heavy rain to northeast Louisiana through the day August 23rd. This flooded roads across portions of the area, and trees in saturated soils were more easily blown down.

events.narrative: Brief heavy rain near El Rancho caused the arroyos to run, and a truck somehow got stuck within the arroyo.
Horseman Park Drive from River Road to Little Valley Elementary was closed due to flash flooding.
Spotter reports total since midnight.
A public report was received of flash flooding at Mesa and Brentwood.

Locally heavy rainfall was reported across York County. A local COOP observer in Hollis measured 4.19 from the 22-23rd. The torrential rainfall caused stream levels to rise on the Middle Branch of the Mousam River in Waterboro. The river washed out a 3 ft diameter culvert and large portion of Scooter Way road.
Spotter reports storm total rainfall.
Heavy rain in New Mexico caused elevated flows in the Gila River downstream as far as Solomon. Floodwaters partially flooded the bridge at Sanchez Rd. along with adjacent lowlands.
Multiple poorly rooted trees were blown due to gusty winds and saturated soils.
Multiple roads were closed or flooded across parts of Franklin Parish.
A tractor trailer hydroplaned and overturned on US Highway 61 south of Blanton Curve. The driver was injured and was transported to a local hospital.
Reports of water and debris over portions of Canal Street near the post office.
Water and debris washed into the road covered portions of Canal Street near the Post Office.
Road closure near Deer Park Ave and Jericho Turnpike in Elwood due to flooding.

A video of a definite funnel cloud was received from near the Mansfield Hollow Dam. |No damage was reported by the Mansfield Emergency Management officials and the broadcast media reported that dam officials reported no damage.  Time estimated by radar.

Video shows road flooding with stranded vehicle on Main Street in Northport NY.
Greenlawn Fire Department reports flooding around town. Little Plains Road closed with several vehicles stranded.
In Cumberland, Abbott Street was flooded and impassable.
In Rehoboth, a CoCoRAHS observer recorded 7.44 inches of rain!  There were a few flooded basements reported.

In East Providence, at 310 PM EDT (210 EST) flash flooding caused the blockage of all travel lanes on Interstate 195 westbound at Exit 2.  At 323 PM EDT (225 PM EST), a car was reportedly stuck in flood waters on Roma Street.  At 402 PM EDT (302 PM EST), Broadway was completely flooded between Juniper and Laura Streets.  Also in East Providence, at 520 PM EDT (420 PM EST), Waterman Avenue was flooded and impassable.
A media reported shared a post on social media indicating that Quebrada Grande was overflowing at PR-404 in Barrio Cruz, Moca.
A site measured 3.70 inches just north of highway 484 in the past 60-90 minutes. A flood warning was in effect.
In South Hadley, multiple trees and wires were down on North Main Street.
The public reported an estimated 4 inches of rain fell between 3:30-5 pm, measured with a rain gauge.
A breach in the berm along Rucker Creek near Bell and Thompson Roads resulted in flash flooding of roadways near the creek in eastern sections of Elfrida.
A flash flood was reported on Big Chino Wash by Yavapai Country Flood Control District. A river gauge on the wash showed a 4.64 foot rise.
Flooding of multiple roads occurred throughout portions of Franklin Parish.
In Central Falls, a car was stuck in flash flooding on Higginson Avenue.  Water was reportedly up to some peoples' knees.
Multiple road closures across Waterbury due to flooding.
Marion County Public Safety reported damage to a residence along Powell Road as the result of thunderstorm winds. A residence had a metal roof pulled from it, and then damaged 3 other nearby homes.
Hail combined with winds gusting to over 70 mph to produce extensive crop damage to lentils, wheat, canola, and corn.
A tree was downed on Grand Avenue resulting in a road closure.
Hail combined with winds gusting to over 70 mph to produce extensive crop damage to lentils, wheat, canola, and corn.
Alachua county 911 call center received a call reporting  street flooding, estimated 6 inches of running water, 10-20 feet wide stream. A Flood warning was in effect.
Broadcast media relayed a video of a waterspout between the Causeway and Mandeville Lakefront.
Mesonet station DW8556 Gainesville measured 2.60 inches of rain within an hour. Flood and Flash Flood Warnings were in effect.
Tree down on wires near Rimmon Hill Road and West Road.
Tree down on wires on Church Street in Beacon Falls CT.
A trained spotter reported a brief funnel cloud.

Alachua county 911 call center received a report that there was 5-6 inches of standing water on NW 16th Ave. They also reported street flooding on the University of Florida campus due to a blocked storm drain and heavy rain. Flood and Flash Flood Warnings were in effect.
The thunderstorm wind gusts combined with dime size hail to cause crop damage.
Northbound 22 entrance ramp to Route 8 in Seymour CT impassible due to flooding.
Mesonet HADS Station FFPC1 1.5 miles west of Forest Falls measured 0.53 inches of rain in 1 hour.
A train spotter reported at 61 MPH wind gust (Davis Weather Station), pea sized hail, and torrential rainfall.
Hail up to one inch in diameter fell in Cottonwood.
East Tepee Street at Plaza and 16th Avenue near Valley and San Marcos in Apache Junction were closed due to debris and downed power poles. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
CHP reported rocks in the middle of lanes along Highway 38 just north of the Forest Falls junction.
The mesonet station at Municipal Yacht Harbor measured a 34 knot thunderstorm wind gust.
Route 8 northbound closed between exits 22 and 23 because of water on road.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated by the public.
The public reported penny sized hail in Duclay.

Flood Control District of Maricopa County Stream Gauge along Apache Trail in Apache Junction broke Alarm Stage at around 1630 MST, with flow peaking at 1.15 feet (38 cfs). This likely caused the intersection of 4th Avenue and Royal Palm Avenue to become impassable. No damages or injuries were reported.
The river gauge on Granite Creek in Prescott measured about a 3 foot rise in about 90 minutes (from 7.40 at 300 PM to 10.35 feet at 430 PM).
Peak wind measured at an NDAWN station at 10 meters.
A teenager was electrocuted by a lightning strike on Roosevelt Blvd resulting in an injury.
Street flooding was reported on Kevin Dr. and Bellair Blvd. About 2.77 inches of rain fell within an hour.
